text.p: SBC Warburg said in a report published Friday that it was recommending Swiss-based freight forwarding concern Danzas as a buy in a model portfolio.
It said that restructuring efforts were expected to pay off, and should start to show up in the company's stated results in the second half of 1996, and fully in 1998.
It gave a target for the concern's participation certificate price at 400 Swiss francs over the next 12 to 18 months. Participation certificates ended on Thursday at 270 Swiss francs.
Its target for registered shares is 2,000 francs compared with 1,460 at Thursday's close.
SBC analysts forecast an ordinary net income target of 76 million Swiss francs for 1998, roughly 3-1/2 times the 1995 figure of 22 million francs.

"After a sweeping reorganisation of operating management over the past year and the initiation of Eurofit, a McKinsey-assisted programme of cost-cutting for its vast European business, Danzas at last looks set to live up to past promise," wrote analysts Mark Browne and Andrew Fitchie.
"Valuation is very depressed versus Swiss industrials and the low-return transport industry," they added.
They said that Danzas has underperformed the Swiss market by 44 percent, and the European transport sector by 27 perecent over the past two years.
"Reorganisation marks a radical break with a 185-year tradition of parochial enterprise," they wrote.
Beyond the low valuation, the analysts also said "we understand the management is reviewing the issue of Danzas's surplus capital." -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
